checks.description: Trace how a caller discovers an operation, feature entry point or known value through IntelliSense and documentation. Evaluate the effort to find existing facilities, not just whether they exist. Verify actual release-matched upstream property types and constants before comparing designs; do not assume a constants class is a typed property.

Trace typical caller code, naming, return values and repeated setup. Inspect model conversions and their receiver/generic constraints, unrelated IntelliSense exposure and ambiguous model names. Compare a plausible compatible improvement with current caller effort using concrete examples, even when the capability already exists.

Compare equivalent routes configured with priority and authentication across feature areas, including actual parameter names/order, named arguments, builder alternatives and declarative attributes. Inspect async naming, cancellation and overloads. Preserve existing signatures, parameter names/order, overload resolution and attribute usage; consider clearer usage guidance or opt-in alternatives.

Trace known/custom string values and typed access to optional payloads. Inspect task/action data with absent payloads, missing keys, empty strings and non-string JSON values; establish fallbacks, exceptions and whether callers can distinguish cases. Compare documented and actual null/empty results for optional information. Preserve existing property types, accepted values and serialized values.

Trace a caller task through routing, generated entry points, contexts, model helpers and Teams client access. Assess required setup, discovery, repeated work and handling of missing information. Inspect existing extension points and generators before evaluating a compatible helper; existing helpers or analyzer rules alone do not prove usability. Keep Teams-specific behavior in MSTeams.

Follow onboarding from imports/configuration to a handler, checking variable definitions, registration location and sample links. Compare XML return/error contracts and defaults with implementation and relevant test assertions, including absent optional data. Review specific API documentation beyond the package README. Documentation corrections must preserve existing runtime behavior.
